best_hook.why: Scarred Duke towers over the usurper and accuses him of selling his soldiers to the enemy: a betrayal accusation that grabs immediately.

best_cliffhanger.why: The fleeing co-conspirator opens the side door and a constable is waiting: escape cut off, arrest not yet made.

must_promos.why: Treason accusation, Crown records proving he was falsely declared dead and his title taken, Rupert screaming and then selling out Sterling, Sterling's sneak exit blocked by the constable; tight, escalating, ends on frozen terror.
Groom screams for an arrest, the guards salute the real Duke instead, a top-secret War Office dossier is read aloud and the traitors are named, cutting as Rupert's own name lands.

standalone_risk: Lord Sterling's role (Catherine's father, Rupert's partner) is never stated, and the military-intelligence exposition (Iberian front, death register) is dense for a cold viewer.
notes: 00:30-00:55 is document-reading exposition; avoid opening a promo there.
